links.reason: Line 6 அறம் நிலைபெற்றோர் அனையேன் makes the delight of the home (wife, son learning பொய்தல்) a state of settled aram, which is Kural 49's அறன் எனப் பட்டதே இல்வாழ்க்கை; with lines 8-9 (வினையும் வேறு புலத்து இலெனே ... யாதனின் பிரிகோ) that state is offered as the reason not to leave, so the pairing does show the maxim used against parting.

The shared term is real: Kural 214 ஒத்தது அறிவான் and the poem's ஒப்புரவு அறியின் (line 8), the townsfolk who would then say அயலோர் ஆகல் (line 10). But the poem does not limit or condition the Kural; it borrows the civic word ironically, so QUALIFIES does not fit, and the teaches sentence is fair but thin.

Kural 1081 அணங்குகொல் ... மாதர்கொல் is the man's silent doubt; Natrinai 155 voices it as a question (அணங்கோ ... நிலைபெற்றனையோ, சொல் இனி மடந்தை, lines 6-8) and records her answer, முறுவல் திறந்தன and tears (lines 9-10). That the smile settles she is a woman is an inference, but a reasonable one, and the contrast of private doubt and spoken question is specific.

Kalittokai 74 line 8-9 நஞ்சு உயிர் செகுத்தலும் அறிந்து உண்டாங்கு ... ஏமுற்றார் brands knowingly eating poison as delusion, while Kural 580 பெயக்கண்டும் நஞ்சுண்டு அமைவர் makes the same knowing act the mark of நாகரிகம். The two value the same act oppositely, and the teaches sentence names what decides it (whom the forbearance is for).

Kural 1247 asks the heart to give up காமம் or நாண்; Ezhupathu 34 line 3 நாணினை நீக்கி உயிரோடு உடன்சென்று pictures the heart giving up நாண் and going with the life. The cost named in teaches rests on உயிரோடு உடன்சென்று, which does read as the life leaving with the heart, so the pair shows one answer to the couplet's choice.

Lines 7 and 13 call both the sacrificial fire and the guests' kitchen fat ஆவுதி, and lines 14-15 (இரண்டு உடன் கமழும் நாற்றமொடு வானத்து நிலைபெறு கடவுளும் விழைதக) make the gods pleased by the kitchen too; the guests are explicit (வருநர் வரையார், விருந்துகண் மாறாது, lines 8-9). Set beside Kural 86's host who becomes a guest of வானத்தவர், the poem gives a concrete link between hospitality and the gods.

Natrinai 306 line 6 சூற் பொறை இறுத்த கோல் தலை இருவி and Akananuru 38 line 13 குலவுப்பொறை யிறுத்த கோல்தலை மருவி are one formula for the reaped millet stubble, and both set the man before it sad (பைதல் ஒரு நிலை, line 8; பைதலன், line 15). The teaches sentence correctly separates the two uses: a warning heard by him versus a pictured grief.
links.text_issue: Akananuru 38 line 13 மருவி is probably இருவி, and line 15 ஐ.தேங்கு is corrupt.

links.reason: The mother's remedy is the stream water (விருந்தின் தீம் நீர் மருந்தும் ஆகும், line 8), and nothing in the poem ties that stream to the lover's hill beyond the kurinji setting (பெரு மலைக் கவாஅன்). Kural 1102's point is that the one who causes the sickness is its cure (தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து); to make the water stand for the man needs a generous reading the Tamil does not fix.

Ainkurunuru 31 only says an oath (சூள்) was sworn at the ford before the bathing companions (உடனாடு ஆயமோடு உற்ற சூளே); it is not an oath sworn by the bathing, and Akananuru 166's lord swears by the Velur god (அணங்குக) to a different woman in a different poem. Two lords' broken oaths do not make two verses with incompatible claims, so TENSION does not fit and teaches misdescribes the first poem.

Kural 1265 says the pallor (பசப்பு) leaves once she sees him கண்ணார; Ainkurunuru 229 reads that rule backwards, inferring a night visit (வந்தனனோ மற்று இரவில்) from the brow's restored beauty (பொன்போல் விறல்கவின் கொள்ளும் நின் நுதலே). The pairing teaches something specific: the cure becomes the evidence.

The swan flying between the southern sea and the Himalaya is distinctive in both: Natrinai 356 தெண் கடல் மேய்ந்த ... செங் கால் அன்னம் ... இமயத்து உச்சி (lines 1-3), Purananuru 67 குமரிஅம் பெருந்துறை அயிரை மாந்தி வடமலைப் பெயர்குவை (lines 6-7). Teaches is accurate that puram sends it as a messenger and akam makes its flight the simile for the heart (போல ... வருந்தினை ... என் உள்ளம், lines 6-7).

Both are Kapilar's and both name Paari's jackfruit hill (பாரி பலவு உறு குன்றம், Natrinai 253 lines 7-8; தீஞ்சுளைப் பலவின், Purananuru 109 line 5). Natrinai's மாரி முற்றிய (line 6), the hill besieged by rain, echoes 109's siege by the three kings, and the girl is அருங் காப்பினள்; since the colophon is வரைவு கடாயது, reading the simile through 109's lesson (தாளின் கொள்ளலிர் ... ஆடினிர் பாடினிர் செலினே) is apt, not forced.

The verses share எழுத்து, and Thirikadugam 56 does put முந்தை எழுத்தின் வரவுணர்ந்து first in a sequence (பிற்பாடு தந்தையும் தாயும்). The teaches sentence is true, but it is a thin observation: Kural 392 ranks letters with numbers as eyes, and the triplet only orders them in time, so little is learned beyond the shared word.

Both rank the beloved's slightest favour above the highest good: Kural 1103 sets துயில் on her arms against தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு, Ainkurunuru 290 sets parrots that are நோக்கவும் படும் ... ஒப்பவும் படுமே above அறம்புரி செங்கோல் மன்னன். Teaches rightly notes the poem pushes both ends further, a glance and a shooing against a just kingdom.

Saying the other woman is favoured is not a claim the other verse contradicts, so TENSION does not fit. And on Ainkurunuru 89's own words (பெண்டென விரும்பின்று அவள்தன் பண்பே) the speaker denies the wife real grace and makes it her mere title, so the claim that each woman says the other has his favour does not hold for this poem, whose sense is in any case uncertain.

Natrinai 210 lines 5-9 deny that grand talk and harsh riding are wealth (செல்வம் அன்று) and define the worthies' wealth as a nature that fears dependants' distress (சேர்ந்தோர் புன்கண் அஞ்சும் பண்பின் மென் கட் செல்வம்), which is close to Kural 241's அருட்செல்வம் set above goods. Teaches is accurate that the friend aims the ranking at a particular husband, narrowing அருள் to fear for the dependant.

Natrinai 378 lines 8-12 name the man who came and broke the girls' sand-house (வரி ஆர் சிறு மனை சிதைஇ வந்து) as the start of the bond; Aimpathu 44 has the girl tell her mother கடல் வந்து என் வண்டல் சிதைத்தது. Given the stock scene, reading her excuse as a coded truth is earned, and the pair teaches it.

Same poet, adjacent decades: 376 curses the fate that sent the girl as அறனில் பால் (line 5), and 393 calls the mother one who அறம்புலந்து பழிக்கும் (line 2), then asks if the daughter has come as ஏமம் for her grieving heart. The verbal tie is real and the reading of the frame is fair, though அண்கணாட்டி is uncertain.

The milk sign is the same in both: Akananuru 48 line 2 பாலும் உண்ணாள் is the symptom the friend explains to the foster mother, and Ainkurunuru 168 line 4 பாலாரும்மே makes drinking milk again depend on the man's grace (நல்கின்). The pairing shows one sign worked two ways, toward the house and toward the lover, as teaches says.

The shared ground is evening's sickness in his absence, which is the common topic. Kural 1226 is about ignorance before he left (அகலாத காலை அறிந்ததிலேன), but Ezhupathu 21's closing எம்மின் மடம்பட்டு வாழ்கிற்பார் இல் is uncertain in sense and does not say she now knows the evening; the contrast teaches builds between excusing ignorance and self-mocked folly is supplied, not in the Tamil.

The hill-as-orchestra figure is distinctive and nearly part for part: Akananuru 82 lines 1-10 (bamboo wind குழலிசை, waterfall முழவு, bees யாழ், monkeys அவை, peacock விறலி) and Paripadal 21 lines 32-36 (மஞ்ஞை ஆட, தும்பி as flute, வண்டினம் யாழ், அருவி as drum). Teaches is right that the Paripadal drops audience and lovers and gives the scene to the god of the drum (இரங்கு முரசினான் குன்று); that it reuses akam rather than sharing a stock figure is a little more than the texts show.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 21 at line 30: a line may have been dropped as a heading (packet flag).

links.reason: The mirage chase is real in both, Aimpathu 36 வெண்தேரை நீராம் என்று எண்ணிப் பிடியோடு ஒருங்கோடி and Akananuru 395 தேர்நசைஇ ஓடிப் புறம்புவழிப் பட்ட ... மேய்பிணைப் பயிரும், and the contrast (the pair fall together, the stag is lost from its doe) is true. But neither verse limits the other, so QUALIFIES is the wrong type; as a shared image used to opposite ends it would be sound.

Kural 1138 says love breaks secrecy and comes into the மன்று; Kalittokai 142 stages it, the girl who once hid her teeth in a smile (முள் நுனை தோன்றாமை முறுவல் கொண்டு, line 7) now laughs so all hear and sings to the சான்றீர். Teaches is accurate that the kali names the second pain the couplet only implies (நலிதரும் காமமும் கௌவையும், line 56).

Kural 1268 வினைகலந்து வென்றீக வேந்தன் is the wish while the king's war goes on, and Kar Narpathu 20 வீறுசால் வேந்தன் வினையும் முடிந்தன is the man after it ends. The before-and-after is true, but nothing limits or conditions the other, and the return after the king's war is the stock mullai situation, so the pair is thin.

The formula is near verbatim: Natrinai 115 மிகப் பேர் அன்பினர் ... நன் புகழ் உலப்பு இன்று பெறினும் தவிரலர் (lines 8-10) and Akananuru 91 பெரும்பேர் அன்பினர் ... குடநாடு பெறினும் தவிரலர் (lines 9-17). Teaches correctly sees the slot filled differently, fame against land, both puram prizes.

The bard as the husband's go-between to other women is real in both (Kalittokai 85 பாண் தலை இட்ட பல வல் புலையனைத் தூண்டிலா விட்டு, lines 22-23; Ezhupathu 50 பொன்னன்னார் சேரியுள் ஓவாது செல் பாண, lines 3-4), but it is the stock marutham situation, and the Ezhupathu verse is uncertain in line 1. The Kalittokai is not needed to explain the venba's order, so the link is thin.

The Pandya name is a real connection: Natrinai 39 முரசு கொண்டு ஓம்பு அரண் கடந்த அடு போர் செழியன் ... கூடல் (lines 8-10) and Purananuru 72 முரசமொடு ஒருங்கு அகப் படேஎன் (lines 8-9). But taking enemy drums is a stock royal deed, the Natrinai does not say which Cheliyan, and the claim that 72's vow 'hardened into a stock epithet' is not shown by the texts.

In the idyll the cane is also crushed by the roaring press (எந்திரம் சிலைக்கும், line 260); it is simply the sugar-mill of a rich land, not a figure for any giver. So the contrast teaches draws with Kural 1078 கரும்புபோல் கொல்லப் பயன்படும் கீழ், the base who give only when crushed, fails, and what is left is the shared word கரும்பு.

Natrinai 80 line 7 தைஇத் திங்கள் தண் கயம் படியும் and Paripadal 11 line 91 தாய் அருகா நின்று தவத் தைந் நீராடுதல் name the same maidens' Thai bath, and the Paripadal shows it as a public rite with priests, elder women (முனித் துறை முதல்வியர்) and mothers. That context does explain the Natrinai girl's தகு நாண் தடைஇ and the setting where he sees her, as teaches says.

Kural 1192 likens the beloved's grace to rain for those who live by it; Kalittokai 71 lines 24-26 take the same figure and measure it: his visit once a year is like ஆராத் துவலை to paddy withering for want of rain (மாரிக்கு அவாவுற்றுப் பீள் வாடும் நெல்). That adds the condition of sufficiency to the Kural's simile, so QUALIFIES fits.

In Ainkurunuru 11 she says நல்லன் while her shoulders say அல்லன் (lines 3-4); in Kural 1236 her shoulders slacken (தொடியொடு தோள்நெகிழ) and it is others calling him கொடியர் that hurts. The pair shows the body's verdict moved from within her to outside readers; the word 'presupposes' in teaches is more than the texts show, but the contrast is real and specific.

Both verses are on the paalai journey for wealth: Kuruntokai 63 gives the heart's reason (ஈதலும் துய்த்தலும் இல்லோர்க்கு இல்), and 331 the friend's barb (நம்மினுஞ் சிறந்த அரும்பொருள்). But 63 already weighs the woman (அம்மா அரிவையும் வருமோ), so 'neither mentions the other's' is not quite right, and the remaining lesson is that the same journey is seen from two sides, which is the shared topic.

The peacock's call in the rains is shared, but it is used differently: in Paripadal 14 lines 8-9 its cry is like the words that call the departed lover (நீடன்மின் வாரும்), while in Akananuru 194 line 15 it calls like girls shooing parrots (கிளிகடி மகளிரின் விளிபடப் பயிரும்) in the season he promised. The rains as a deadline is a common convention rather than something this Akananuru poem uniquely supplies, so the tie is thin though the teaches sentence is true.

Same decade and the same worship of the hill god: 257 குன்றக் குறவன் கடவுட் பேணி இரந்தனன் பெற்ற, and 259 the daughter மலையுறை கடவுள் குலமுதல் வழுத்தி. But 259 does not say what she prays for, and her brimming eyes (கலிழ்ந்த கண்ணள்) are unexplained, so 'a love of her own to pray for' is supplied and teaches does not hold.

The Korkai neythal is shared: Ainkurunuru 188 கொற்கையம் பெருந்துறை வைகறை மலரும் நெய்தல் for eyes in beauty, Natrinai 23 கொற்கை முன்துறைச் ... நெய்தல் ... தொலைந்த கண்ணே for eyes faded. Opposite uses of one image are not incompatible claims, so TENSION is the wrong type; as a same_image link teaches holds.

Kural 610 is about மடி (sloth) in a king, who wins the earth அடியளந்தான் தாஅயது; Kural 1103 asks whether தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு is sweeter than sleep on the beloved's arms. Sleep is not named in 610 (it relies on 605 outside the link), the two Vishnu measures are different things, and different advice for a king's duty and a lover's delight is not a tension.

Kural 1188 has the town see her pallor (பசந்தாள் இவள்) but no one name its cause; Ainkurunuru 225 asks whether the lover himself does not perceive it (ஓரார் கொல் நம் காதலோரே, line 5). The pair specifically shows the symptom seen by everyone except the man it is for.

Ainkurunuru 93's bees come to her hair after buffalo graze the flowers (lines 1-2), and line 3 (செய்த இனைய மன்ற) is hard, so whether the bees' turn to her crown is a verdict on its fragrance is unclear. Kuruntokai 2's question to the bee (நறியவும் உளவோ நீயறியும் பூவே) is a real echo, but the claim that 93 answers it rests on a generous reading.
links.text_issue: Ainkurunuru 93 line 3 is hard to construe (marker flag).

links.reason: Puram 42's தானையும் கடலென முழங்கும் is a common simile, and Thinaimalai 52 reverses it (திரை பாகனாகத் திமில் களிறாக ... வேந்து கிளர்ந்தன்ன). The reversal is true, but the argument for marriage comes from the venba's own விரையாது and நாள் ஆய்ந்து வரைதல் அறம், not from anything in Purananuru 42, so the pairing adds little.

Both idylls lay the lute's leather cover like a line of fine hair on a woman's belly with the same verb: Porunaratruppadai lines 6-7 இளஞ்சூற் செய்யோள் அவ்வயிற்று ஐதுமயிர் ஒழுகிய தோற்றம் போல, and Malaipadukadam lines 30-32 வதுவை நாறும் ... மடந்தை ... அடங்குமயிர் ஒழுகிய அவ்வாய் கடுப்ப. Teaches is accurate that it is a bards' set figure varied in the woman's stage of life.

Verse 7 defines the four எச்சில் (இயக்கம் இரண்டும் இணைவிழைச்சு வாயின் விழைச்சு) and verse 8 takes up நால்வகை எச்சிலும் with three prohibitions (ஓதார் உரையார் வளராரே) and a reward (மேதைகள் ஆகுறுவார்). The definition-then-rule sequence and the reward in learning are in the Tamil.

Natrinai 294 lines 1-2 தீயும் வளியும் விசும்பு பயந்தாங்கு நோயும் இன்பமும் ஆகின்று make the man's chest both the sickness and the joy, one source for both, which is Kural 1102's தன்நோய்க்குத் தானே மருந்து. The colophon places it in the wedding house (மணமனையுள்), so teaches' move from private wonder to public confirmation is grounded.

Both set the girls driving birds from the fish laid out to dry: Thinaimalai 44 படும்புலால் புட்கடிவான் புக்க, Akananuru 80 பல்மீன் உணங்கல் படுபுள் ஓப்புதும். Akananuru 80 says outright that the day meeting replaces the night crossing (பகல் வந்தீமே), while the venba only names the grove as her place, so the long poem spells out what the short one implies.

iraicchi.act: the old stag bends down the tall tree for its hungry doe, eats only what is left, and stands as shade for its fawn
iraicchi.sense: on the road he took he will see the stag caring for its mate and young, so the friend assures her he has great desire for her and will return

poems.note: The blue lily is only looked at; it does nothing.
The bards who lost Evvi are an open simile (போல).
Trampled neythal could stand for the girl's spoiled beauty, but no second firm correspondence and lines 9-12 are hard.

iraicchi.act: the doe with its new-born fawn feeds in the rain-fed field
iraicchi.sense: if the man sees creatures keeping their young in the promised season he will remember her and come back before her bangles slip

poems.note: The peerkku flowers are a token whose colour and season speak; they perform no act.
The opening lotus and ambal invite a hidden reading, but the flower is joined to a face by போல and no two firm pairs can be named.
The brothers' act is a human trait stated openly, not a native vehicle.
The cloud is addressed directly; striking it removes the poem.
The crocodile is a literal danger of the path.

ullurai.anchor: ஊரன் பெண்டினை யாயிற் பலவா குகநின் நெஞ்சிற் படரே

poems.note: Fish = the lord, the ripe cane fruit snatched = the women he takes; the second pair is close to the first.
The care is the charioteer's, not the crab's act.
The sky's laughter is an open simile (நகுவதுபோல்) of mood.

iraicchi.act: the wet crab, afraid of the playing girls, runs off into the sea
iraicchi.sense: like the crab the lover now keeps away from her company, since even their laughing play is forbidden

poems.note: Hard: the restriction is the guardians', and the crab's flight is a light hint.

iraicchi.act: the young cow-elephant strokes the back of her exhausted, bewildered tusker so that he can at last sleep
iraicchi.sense: on his own hill mates tend each other in distress, which measures the bond the man has let slacken

poems.note: Every spring image is joined to her state by போலும்.
The poem states its moral itself (lines 3-4).
The kaanthal from his hill = the man, planting it at home = bringing him into the house; the plant is also literal, which makes the call hard.
